title: Any client account can list all customers' personal and payment details via /admin/customers
summary: GET /api/admin/customers returns HTTP 200 with every customer record to client users of two different companies; the config says only admins may see customers. Records include contact name, email, phone, national ID, address and card last-4 fields.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
GET /api/admin/customers (see evidence for the exact request)
Observe HTTP 200 with the full customer list
Repeat as bright-1 (a different company): same result
actual: HTTP 200 with all customers' records, including personal-data field names such as email, phone, cnic, address, card_last4
suspected_cause: The customers route lacks the admin-role check that the reports route has

regression_test.description: As a client, GET /api/admin/customers and expect 403

title: A client can read another company's orders by id
summary: GET /api/orders/{id} returns 200 and the full order to a user of a different company. The Client Portal order page also shows it when the id is changed in the URL. The list and search endpoints are correctly scoped.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 and place a QA- order, note its id
Sign in as bright-1 (or zain-1) and GET /api/orders/{id}
Observe HTTP 200 with the Acme order
In the Client Portal as zain-1, open order.html?id=<that id>: the order page loads
actual: HTTP 200 with the order body; the UI page title and content show the other company's order
suspected_cause: Order detail looks up by id without filtering on the caller's company

regression_test.description: Client A creates an order; client B GET /orders/{id} expects 403/404

title: Signing out does not revoke the API token
summary: POST /auth/logout returns 204, but the same token keeps working on /me and /orders afterwards, against the rule that signing out ends the session at once.
steps: Sign in as zain-1 over the API
POST /api/auth/logout (204)
GET /api/me with the same token
GET /api/orders with the same token
Observe HTTP 200 for both
suspected_cause: Logout does not invalidate the token server-side; the UI only clears local storage

regression_test.description: Logout then GET /me with the same token expects 401

title: Tax is charged on the pre-discount subtotal, so discounted orders are overcharged
summary: For orders at or above 1,000.00 the discount is correct but tax is 10% of the full subtotal instead of the discounted subtotal, so totals are too high.
steps: Sign in as acme-1
POST /api/orders with 100 x p-101 and 100 x p-104 (subtotal 1,000.00)
Observe discount 50.00, tax 100.00, total 1,050.00
In the Client Portal, order 12 x Printer Toner Cartridge: confirmation shows Total $1,133.88
expected: Subtotal 1,000.00: discount 50.00, tax 95.00, total 1,045.00. For 12 toner (1,079.88): total 1,128.48
actual: Total 1,050.00 for the 1,000.00 order (tax 100.00); UI shows $1,133.88 for the toner order (tax 107.99)
suspected_cause: Tax is computed from the subtotal rather than subtotal minus discount

regression_test.description: Order with subtotal 100000 cents expects discount 5000, tax 9500, total 104500

title: Orders accept empty item lists and out-of-range or fractional quantities, including negative totals
summary: POST /api/orders returns 201 for an empty items array and for quantity 0, -3, 1001 and 1.5. A quantity of -3 creates an order with a negative total. Rules require a whole number from 1 to 1,000 and at least one item.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
POST /api/orders with items[0].quantity = -3 (see evidence)
Observe HTTP 201 with total_cents -2145
Repeat with items = [], quantity 0, 1001 and 1.5: all 201
actual: HTTP 201 and the order is stored (negative order total visible in My Orders)
suspected_cause: No quantity or items validation in the order handler

regression_test.description: POST orders with each invalid quantity and empty items; expect 400

title: Client's order list shows a stale status after an admin changes it
summary: After an admin moves an order forward, GET /orders/{id} shows the new status but the client's list (GET /orders) keeps showing 'placed', including after a reload and again after the admin changes it a second time.
steps: As acme-1 read GET /orders (warm)
As admin PATCH /admin/orders/{id}/status to processing (also done via the Admin Portal)
As acme-1 GET /orders/{id}: processing
As acme-1 GET /orders?q=<reference>: still placed
expected: List and detail agree straight away
actual: Detail says processing/shipped; list says placed
suspected_cause: Order list is cached per company and not invalidated on status change

regression_test.description: Warm list, change status as admin, list expects the new status

title: GET /orders returns HTTP 500 for page_size=0 and for q=( or q=\
summary: Zero page size and search text containing a regex special character crash the list endpoint.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
GET /api/orders?page_size=0, then ?q=( and ?q=\ (see evidence)
Observe HTTP 500 each time
expected: HTTP 400 for page_size=0; 200 with matches (or none) for special-character searches
suspected_cause: Search text is used as a regular expression unescaped; page_size=0 causes a bad calculation

title: Malformed JSON responses expose a stack trace and server file paths
summary: Sending invalid JSON to POST /auth/login or POST /orders returns 400 with a stack trace and server source paths in the body.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with a malformed JSON body (see evidence)
Observe the 400 body contains a stack field and file paths
Same on POST /api/orders
expected: A short error message without internals
actual: Body includes stack trace and server paths

regression_test.description: Malformed JSON expects 400 without 'stack' or file paths

title: My Orders on mobile (390px): first row hidden under the toolbar and Total column cut off
summary: At 390x844 the first order row sits about 22px under the Status/New order toolbar, and the table scrolls sideways (438px in 359px) with the Total column clipped and no visible cue.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
Resize to 390x844
Open My orders
Observe the first row's reference is covered and totals are cut off
Reload and repeat: same
expected: All rows and totals visible without overlap
suspected_cause: Toolbar overlaps the table (negative margin or fixed height) and table has fixed min-width

regression_test.description: Visual check at 390px that the first row is not covered

title: Controls without accessible names: product dropdown, admin search, refresh and clear buttons
summary: The New order product select (Client Portal) and the Admin Orders search box (placeholder only) and the refresh and clear-filter icon buttons have no accessible name.
steps: Open Client Portal New order and run the page audit: unnamedControls lists the product select
Open Admin Portal Orders and run the audit: search, refresh and clear buttons listed
expected: Every control has a label or aria-label

regression_test.description: Accessibility check that all form controls have names

title: Sales report takes about 4 seconds to load
summary: GET /admin/reports/sales consistently takes about 4 s while other calls take a few ms.
steps: Sign in as admin
GET /api/admin/reports/sales twice
Observe 4003 ms and 4010 ms
suspected_cause: Artificial delay or an unindexed aggregate

title: page_size=-1 is accepted and echoed back in GET /orders
summary: A negative page size returns 200 with page_size -1, which breaks the documented minimum of 1.
steps: GET /api/orders?page_size=-1 as acme-1
Observe HTTP 200 and page_size -1 in the body

title: Two simultaneous identical order submissions both create orders
summary: Sending the same POST /orders twice at once returns 201 for both. I am unsure whether duplicates are intended, as there is no idempotency key in the spec.
steps: POST /api/orders twice in parallel with identical QA- body (see evidence)
Observe two 201 responses
expected: A single order, or a documented duplicate guard

regression_test.description: Parallel identical POSTs create at most one order
